questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to make your own Halloween costume
The history of American horror films
Whether Halloween costumes are too scary
Why pumpkins are so popular in autumn
questions.why: Neil says they'll discuss whether Halloween is no longer harmless fun.

questions.q: What is Neil wearing at the start?
options: A bedsheet with holes for his eyes
A creepy clown mask with red hair
A witch's hat and a long black dress
A Grim Reaper cloak and a skull mask
questions.why: Sam says he's wearing a white bedsheet over his head with two holes cut out for his eyes.

questions.q: What did the ancient festival of Samhain celebrate?
options: The end of a long war with the Romans
The start of the new year in spring
The birth of a king and his family
Changing seasons, when the dead came near
questions.why: Sam says it celebrated the changing of the seasons, when the dead could contact the living.

questions.q: Why did online shops remove some Halloween costumes?
options: They were too expensive for most families
Parents said they were too frightening
They didn't sell well in the shops
They were unsafe to wear near fire
questions.why: Shops removed costumes like creepy clown masks after parents complained they were too frightening.

questions.q: What does Joanne O'Connell think shops are doing?
options: Racing to sell the grimmest outfits
Selling only costumes for adults
Trying hard to protect young children
Making costumes more traditional again
questions.why: She says retailers are in a race to the bottom for the grimmest outfit so they can make money.

questions.q: What is Neil's first reaction to the parents' complaints?
options: He completely agrees with the parents
He wants to ban Halloween in schools
He thinks it's too far; it should be scary
He says he's never been scared at all
questions.why: He says, 'Isn't this going too far? I mean, Halloween is supposed to be scary!'

options: Banning all scary costumes in shops
A halfway house that protects young children
Letting children wear whatever they want
Only celebrating Halloween at home
questions.why: She thinks there's 'a sort of a halfway house' – scary is fine for teens, but young children need protecting.

questions.q: What does Neil decide at the end?
options: To buy a scarier costume
To stop celebrating Halloween
To stay at home
To keep his simple ghost costume
questions.why: He says he'll stick with his bedsheet ghost.
